why: P2 #4 of the external audit, and the only case in this module that is not about the rule: it is about what the rule CAN SEE. `semComentarioNemImport` was two regex substitutions with no notion of a string, so a block opener INSIDE A STRING opened a comment that only closed at the file's next block closer -- and erased everything in between. Measured across rebar's 139 code files: 9 had code outside the examination, the worst with 1,181 tokens. Here the fail side has `rejectUnauthorized: false` between a string with a block opener and the JSDoc that closes it; with the old remover that side goes GREEN, which is a false negative, the worst outcome for a ruler. The pass side has the SAME string and the SAME JSDoc, and no disabled defense: it is the one that guarantees the fix did not turn into accusing a string with a slash and an asterisk inside.
